The median home in Bedford Park was built in 1947. Across the 200 housing units here, 92 percent went up before 1980 and 42 percent date to 1939 or earlier. That single figure decides more about a paint job than anything else anyone will ask you on the phone.

Behind the housing are 161 owner households and 35 renter households, 82.1 percent owner occupied. Ranked against the 54 suburbs and towns covered here, Bedford Park lands in the top four on the highest detached-house share (98 percent, first of them all), the largest prewar share (42 percent, first of them all) and the oldest housing by median build year (1947, first of them all). It is also near the top for the smallest housing stock overall (200 units), the smallest owner-occupied market (161 households) and the largest share built before 1970 (92 percent). This is a very small market: 200 housing units in total, so every estimate on this page is a thin one and should be read as a direction rather than a measurement.

Lead-safe work on Bedford Park houses

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 92 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Bedford Park. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Bedford Park at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 6.1-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Bedford Park.

None of that is a reason to leave a Bedford Park house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Certification is a document, not a sentence on a website. It shows as pending below because no number has been supplied. Ask to see it, in Bedford Park and everywhere else.

Bedford Park against its nearest neighbor

Clearing is 0.8 miles from Bedford Park and is the closest comparison there is. It is not a close one. The two differ on prewar share (42 percent against 9.5 percent); owner households (161 against 6,618); share of units in buildings of two or more (2 percent against 34.1 percent).

Why two houses in Bedford Park do not price the same

With 42 percent of Bedford Park prewar and a 1947 median, the ceilings are the part people forget. Old plaster ceilings move, they have usually been patched at least once, and a flat white over the top of that shows every previous repair the moment the light comes across it. They are worth pricing as their own line. 161 households own in Bedford Park and 35 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

The lines a quote for Bedford Park needs to show

  • Plaster as well as drywall. 42 percent of Bedford Park is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6.1 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.
  • Whole elevations. 98 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Distance, stated. Bedford Park is 2.6 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Bedford Park is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is brick bungalow, Cape Cod and early ranch. The walls are masonry, so exterior paint concentrates in trim, soffit, fascia, garage surround and doors. Bedford Park interiors are trim-heavy for their square footage.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1947 median build year, and the split between 98 percent detached houses, 0 percent attached homes and 2 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Bedford Park is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Questions

Asked about Bedford Park

Is the $266,800 median home value in Bedford Park what a job here costs?

They are two different things. $266,800 is a published estimate of home value in Bedford Park and nothing more. Cost of work depends on what is on the walls now, how much trim there is and what has to come off before anything goes on, and none of that is knowable from a median.

Who actually shows up in Bedford Park?

Our crew, with Mike Walsh running it. He owns the company, and every job is quoted after we walk it. Tell us the town, the room and roughly what you want, and you will know what happens next on the same call. 708-935-4289.

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes, and on 6.1-room housing it is often the right call. Doing one room properly beats doing four at a pace that shows, and it spreads the cost across seasons rather than across a credit card. Say that is what you want when you call, because it changes how the work is sequenced.

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 6.1 median rooms and a 1947 median build year in Bedford Park the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.
